deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT (from fol. 3v). Put X = 1 + x^4/10 + x^8/24 + 5x^12/208 + 35x^16/2176 + 3x^20/256. These are the terms of the series for the lemniscatic arc: binom(2n,n)/4^n/(4n+1) gives 1/10, 1/24, 5/208, 35/2176, 63/5376 = 3/256. So z = xX = ∫_0^x dt/sqrt(1-t^4) = arcsl x, and x = sl z. Gauss uses his Lagrange-inversion rule (art. 4 of the previous page): coefficient of z^{4k} in log x = (coefficient of x^{4k} in X^{-4k})/(4k). Earlier he had found log sl z = log z - z^4/10 + z^8/300 - z^12/4875 + 127 z^16/(65000·153).

PART 1. Coefficient of z^20 in log sl z (top half of the page). Write X = 1 + w. Then a5 = (1/20)·[x^20] Σ_k binom(-20,k) w^k. Term by term:
- k=1: -20·(3/256).
- k=2: binom(-20,2) = 210, and [x^20]w^2 = 2·(1/10)(35/2176) + 2·(1/24)(5/208). Gauss writes these as 210·35·2/(10·2176) and 210·5·2/(24·208).
- k=3: -(20·21·22/6) = -1540, times [x^20]w^3 = 3·(1/100)(5/208) + 3·(1/10)(1/576).
- k=4: +(20·21·22·23/24) = 8855, times [x^20]w^4 = 4·(1/1000)(1/24).
- k=5: -(20·…·24/120) = -42504, times 1/10^5.

Reduced, the bracket is
-15/2^6 + 735/(17·2^6) + 175/(13·2^5) - 231/208 - 77/96 + 1771/1200 - 5313/12500.

Grouping:
- -15/64 + 735/1088 = 15/34.
- 175/416 - 77/96 = (525 - 1001)/1248 = -119/312 (scratch: 525, 1001, 476).
- -231/208 + 1771/1200 = (23023 - 17325)/15600 = 2849/7800 (scratch: 23023, 17325, 5698).
- -119/312 + 2849/7800 = (-2975 + 2849)/7800 = -21/1300.

The common denominator for 15/34 - 21/1300 - 5313/12500 is 221·12500 = 2762500 (circled on the page). The numerators are:
- 15·13·6250 = 1218750;
- 21·2125 = 44625;
- 5313·221 = 1174173 (scratch 5313, 10626, 10626 → 1174173).

Since 44625 + 1174173 = 1218798, the bracket is -48/2762500. Then a5 = -48/(20·2762500) = -3/3453125 = -3/(221·15625). Result line:
log sl z = log z - z^4/10 + z^8/300 - z^12/4875 + 127 z^16/(65000·153) - 3 z^20/(221·15625).

PART 2. lQ. From the a_k Gauss writes
lQ = z^4/12 - z^8/280 + z^12/4950 - z^16/78000 + 41 z^20/(342·221·625).
The marginal factors 5, 15, 65(=5·13), 255, 3·1025 → 41 show the rule used: b_k = -a_k((-4)^k - 1)/((-4)^k - 2). That is, the factors are 5/6, 15/14, 65/66, 255/254, 1025/1026, with (1+i)^4 = -4.

My derivation of the rule (not on the page): it is equivalent to B((1+i)z) - 2B(z) = A(z) - A((1+i)z), where A = log(sl z/z) and B = log Q. By the complex-multiplication formula sl((1+i)z) = (1+i) sl z/sl'z, the right side equals log sl'(z) = ½ log(1 - sl^4 z). Hence Q((1+i)z)^2 = Q^4 - P^4 with P = sl·Q. This Q is Gauss's lemniscatic denominator function: sl = P/Q with Q = 1 + 2z^4/4! - …, P = z - 2z^5/5! + ….

Below lQ he factors 280·5/8 = 1·5·7·5, 4950·5/2 = 5·9·11·25, 78000·45/16 = 9·13·15·125, and 342·221·625·(18/41)… = 13·17·19·625. The struck 8/15, 2/7, 55/18 and the final 5/8, 5/2, 45/16, 41/18 look like an unsuccessful search for a closed pattern in the b_k.

PART 3. Coefficients of Q = exp(lQ) in factorial form (bottom). The terms written are:
- b5 = 41/(13·17·18·19·625);
- b4·q1 = -1/(72000·13);
- b3·q2 = -1/(8000·11·7·81), with q2 = -4/8! = -1/10080;
- b2·q3 = -408/(12!·280), with q3 = 408/12!;
- b1·q4 = 13584/(16!·12), with q4 = 13584/16!.

So Q = 1 + 2z^4/4! - 4z^8/8! + 408 z^12/12! + 13584 z^16/16! + …. q3 and q4 check exactly.

He then puts these terms over the common denominator 19·17·13·11·7·5^4·3^6·2^13 (bottom line; continued on fol. 4v, where 41·77·81·4096 = 1047416832 and the 4199 = 13·17·19 products appear) to get q5·20!. The correct recursion is 5q5 = 5b5 + 4b4q1 + 3b3q2 + 2b2q3 + b1q4. My own completion (not on the page) gives q5 = -2911/(5·2^13·3^6·5^3·7^2·11·13·17·19), i.e. q5·20! = -838368.
errors: Not an error on the page as such: the image/transcription reading '1/4975' for the z^12 coefficient must be 1/4875 (as on fol. 3v). This is consistent with lQ's 1/4950 = (1/4875)(65/66) and with my recomputation.

The bottom sum lists b5, b4q1, b3q2, b2q3, b1q4 without visible weights 5,4,3,2,1 (or the 1/5). If it is summed unweighted as written, it would not give the z^20 coefficient of exp(lQ). It is unclear whether the weights are supplied in the marginal numbers; the computation is completed on the next page.
All arithmetic checked in parts 1 and 2 is correct: the z^20 coefficient is -3/3453125, and b2..b5 follow exactly from the stated rule.

results.what: Lagrange-inversion computation of the z^20 coefficient of log sl z: log sl z = log z - z^4/10 + z^8/300 - z^12/4875 + 127z^16/9945000 - 3z^20/3453125
results.modern_name: Taylor expansion of log of the lemniscatic sine via Lagrange–Bürmann inversion
results.usually_credited_to: Lagrange (inversion formula, 1770); lemniscatic sine expansions: Gauss (1797–99, Werke III)

results.what: Coefficients of log Q obtained from those of log sl via b_k = -a_k((-4)^k-1)/((-4)^k-2), i.e. Q((1+i)z)^2 = Q^4 - P^4 (complex multiplication by 1+i)
results.modern_name: Functional equation of the lemniscatic sigma/theta-type function under complex multiplication by 1+i
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (lemniscatic P,Q functions, unpublished, Werke III); sigma function: Weierstrass

results.modern_name: Power series of the denominator function in sl = P/Q (essentially a lemniscatic sigma/theta function)

deep.surprise_reason: Gauss's lemniscatic functions P, Q with sl = P/Q and their factorial-form series are known from his Nachlass (Werke III). This page is a computational worksheet extending the coefficients to z^20 using the 1+i multiplication relation. It is a nice concrete witness of his method but not a new result.

checkable.asserts: The reduced bracket gives the z^20 coefficient of log sl z.
Lagrange-inversion coefficient of z^20 in log x, where z = x*X.
z = x*X is the lemniscatic arc integral, so x = sl z.
The lQ coefficients follow from the log sl coefficients by the (1+i)-multiplication rule.
Factorial-form coefficients of Q; the last value is my completion of the page's computation.
